children: Dividends are rising faster than corporate capital spending, marking a sharp change from the late-1990s period when dividends accounted for a much smaller share of companies’ capital expenditure, according to TS Lombard.
“Although firms are raising capex these past few quarters, dividends are rising faster,” TS Lombard's Steven Blitz said in a post shared by Daily Chartbook.
Blitz pointed to the historical relationship between dividends and capital expenditure, noting that dividends were about 20% of capex during the late 1990s, compared with close to 50% today.
The chart showed the dividends-to-capex ratio generally in the 20%-40% range through the 1990s and 2000s, with sharp temporary dips around 2005 and 2017, before climbing toward 50% recently.

title: Capex rises, but dividends are growing faster
